at_sea: TICKET 1c4ae8f053fe (a-seal-snapshots-cairn-once-per-batch) is at PROVEME and KICKED BACK at /sail step 6 — the build is done, proven, sealed, committed and pushed (cairn fc67433), but the chart cannot be answered and PROVED cannot be crossed. THE BUILD: the tester's instance seal now (1) copies the trail tree EMPTY but PRESENT, (2) reads the live instance root ONCE per process into a pristine that every proof copies from, (3) takes ONE copy per proof instead of two because the seal probe clears its own marker, and (4) records what the sandbox cost in evidence.instance_seal.scratch on every seal. Measured on this box in one minute: 888.7MB/9.28s/163,352 entries per sealed proof BEFORE (HEAD's own isolation.py loaded as a live module and run), 118.0MB/0.34s/3,620 entries for a batch's first proof and 0.09s for each one after. cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_isolation.py carries 14 teeth, green twice, and all six new ones bite under mutation. THE KICK-BACK: the validate berth's second criterion is 'no proof depended on the old copy'. Re-seal sweep of the whole corpus = 200 proofs, 192 green, 8 red. Attribution was MEASURED: the tree was stashed, HEAD c9db255 confirmed to carry the old two-copy code, all 8 re-run there — 7 are red at HEAD too. The 8th, cairn/devices/inference_domain/proofs/test_an_inference_call_logs_that_it_started.py, was green at HEAD and is red now. So the criterion is recorded FAILED, and the verdict door (codemother/machines/verdict) REFUSES to berth a failed criterion at all: 'a failed criterion is a kick-back, not a crossing'. That refusal is the physics working, not an obstacle to route around.
next_direction: AKIEN'S RULING IS THE ONE THING BLOCKING TIER 1. The 8th red is a HOLLOW GREEN the change exposed, not a regression it caused: survey_the_corpus in cairn/devices/inference_domain/probes/an_inference_call_logs_that_it_started.py:129 resolves the trail through TWO doors and only the first follows the device — line 143 asks domain.diagnostic_trail() (honours _diagnostic_roots, moves when a proof moves the world) and sets trail_exists from it; line 148 builds BreadcrumbLog('inference_domain', 0) with NO roots, re-deriving the LIVE logs berth, and reads the records from THERE. The tooth test_the_probe_reads_the_address_the_device_declares writes ONE line into an isolated trail and asserts trail_misses >= 1 — it has been passing on the live trail's historical lines, never on the line it wrote. Verbatim the failure the function's own docstring says it exists to prevent. Three measurements pin it: sealed at HEAD green, sealed now red (trail_exists=True, post_era_lines=0, trail_misses=0), UNSEALED now green. THE QUESTION FOR HIM, two readings and I recommend the first: (a) FIX IT — the honest fix needs a public 'read the trail at this path' seam, i.e. a diagnostic_records() sibling to diagnostic_trail() in cairn/tools/base/diagnostic.py, which is an addition to the basemost class every device inherits and to another device's probe. Outside 1c4ae8f053fe's constrain bounds (in: ro-bind aider data, empty writable logs, one snapshot per batch, reflink copy, du in evidence), and /sail step 2 says wanting something out is his question, never a silent widening. (b) RULE THE CRITERION as meaning 'no proof LEGITIMATELY depended on the old copy', pass it, cross PROVED, and let the probe's defect ride its own ticket. THEN: finish tier 1 — d0f2b03952e3, 4d9115eb04cd, 8754ae677af6, feeb4c786b14 (PROVEME:waiting), 1accdc1781aa (BUILDME:queued) — then tiers 2-4.
